transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. How can I help you today?

Hi Dr. Smith. I've been feeling incredibly restless lately, like I constantly have to be moving around. It's gotten to the point where I feel this uncontrollable urge to pace, climb, or run around even when I'm supposed to be sitting still.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, especially in situations where you're expected to sit still, like at work or during meetings?

Yes, definitely. During meetings or when I'm at my desk, I get this intense inner restlessness that makes it almost impossible to just sit still. I feel a constant, nagging urge to get up and pace around, and it's really hard to ignore.
Do you often act without thinking, such as blurting out answers before questions are finished or interrupting others during conversations?
I don't think I do that very often. I'm not really sure, but I don't recall having a habit of interrupting others or blurting out answers before they finish.
Have these symptoms of restlessness and difficulty sitting still been present since childhood, or did they start more recently?

Yes, these feelings have actually been around for as long as I can remember. I distinctly recall being constantly restless and unable to sit still in class way back in elementary school, definitely before I was 12. It has just persisted for my entire life.
Has this restlessness significantly interfered with your work, relationships, or daily activities?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't given much thought to how it interferes with my work or relationships, since I'm mostly just focused on how uncomfortable the constant feeling itself is.

Can you think of any specific situations at work, in social settings, or at home where your restlessness has caused problems, such as difficulty concentrating, completing tasks, or maintaining relationships?

I definitely experience that constant restlessness, but I'm not really sure if it has caused specific problems with concentrating, completing tasks, or my relationships. I haven't really thought about it affecting those areas, as I'm usually just focused on the physical urge to move.
Do you ever feel an overwhelming need to move that is accompanied by a sense of inner tension or anxiety, and does moving provide temporary relief?

Yes, I definitely experience a strong sense of inner restlessness and a constant urge to move, especially when I am expected to remain still. Getting up to walk around or even just changing my seating position really helps to relieve that physical tension. It feels like the only way to get some temporary relief.
Are there times when your restlessness significantly worsens, such as during periods of stress, or does it remain consistently present regardless of circumstances?
I'm not quite sure, to be honest. I haven't really paid attention to whether my stress levels make it worse, or if the restlessness is just consistently there all the time.
Does your restlessness tend to improve when you're engaged in highly stimulating or physically active tasks, or does it persist even during those times?
I'm not quite sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about whether highly stimulating or physically active tasks make the restlessness improve or if it just stays the same.
Do you also experience any symptoms of anxiety, such as excessive worry, nervousness, or physical symptoms like rapid heartbeat or sweating, especially when you're unable to move?

I don't think I experience anxiety or excessive worry, and I've never noticed physical symptoms like a rapid heartbeat or sweating. For me, it really feels more like a physical restlessness and just needing to move.
